title: The Secrets of Persuasion
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.answer: D — investigate whether persuasion has a scientific basis
questions.answerKey: D — investigate whether persuasion has a scientific basis
questions.translation: Cialdini 的研究和寫作主要目的是什麼？

blocks.text: “The main purpose of Cialdini’s research and writing is to…”
這是 Multiple Choice。題目問 main purpose，所以不能只抓文章中的一個例子，例如 towels、salespeople、sales-training programmes。要找 Cialdini 整體研究方向。
“Cialdini’s towel experiments (more of them later) are part of his research into how we persuade others to say yes.”
Cialdini 的毛巾實驗是他研究我們如何說服別人答應的一部分。

“All my life I’ve been an easy mark for the blandishments of salespeople and fundraisers and I’d always wondered why they could get me to buy things I didn’t want and give to causes I hadn’t heard of,” says Cialdini on the phone from London, where he is promoting his latest book.
Cialdini 說，他一生都很容易受銷售員和籌款者的花言巧語影響，所以一直想知道為何他們能令自己買不想要的東西，或捐錢給自己未聽過的機構。只看首尾句，可以先猜 Paragraph B 的功能是介紹 Cialdini 研究 persuasion 的大方向：他想知道人為何會答應、為何會被影響、這些影響技巧是否可以被整理成科學原則。
題目中最有定位力的字是：“main purpose”
“research into how we persuade others to say yes”
“systematising the principles and methods of persuasion and writing bestsellers about them”
這些字把答案帶到 Paragraph B。尤其 “systematising the principles and methods” 和 “applying a little science” 表明，他並非單純研究銷售員，也非只教人賣貨，他在研究 persuasion 背後是否有可整理、可驗證、可應用的科學原理。

“While he’s anxious not to be seen as the man who’s written the bible for snake-oil salesmen, for decades the Arizona State University social psychology professor has been systematising the principles and methods of persuasion and writing bestsellers about them.”
雖然他很不想被視為替騙子銷售員寫下聖經的人，但這位亞利桑那州立大學社會心理學教授數十年來一直在系統整理說服的原則和方法，並撰寫相關暢銷書。

這句有三個重點。第一，Cialdini 是 social psychology professor，研究身份屬於心理學。第二，他systematising principles and methods，即把 persuasion 的原則和方法整理成系統。第三，他不想被看成 snake-oil salesmen 的導師，這直接排除 C「help people sell products」這種太狹窄甚至帶有負面方向的理解。
A explain why researchers should conduct studies in real-world settings這只符合 Paragraph C 的部分方法。Cialdini 確實走出實驗室做 real-world research，但這只是方法，不是 research and writing 的 main purpose。
B discover why some people become successful salespeople文章有提到 cold-caller、salespeople、sales-training programmes，但他研究的範圍比salespeople 大，還包括父母、酒店住客、餐廳客人、慈善捐款、權威、喜歡、一致性等。
C help people sell products原文特別說他 “anxious not to be seen as” 替 snake-oil salesmen 寫聖經的人。C 把研究目的壓縮成銷售產品，範圍過窄。
D investigate whether persuasion has a scientific basis正確。原文的 “science of persuasion”、“social psychology professor”、“systematising the principles and methods” 都指向 persuasion 背後有可研究的科學基礎。
research into how we persuade others to say yes= investigate persuasion systematising the principles and methods= 尋找可整理的規律applying a little science= scientific basis
最容易被 C 吸引，因為文章多次出現 salespeople、cold-caller、sell automobiles、sell insurance。可是這些是研究材料和例子，真正控制答案的是 “science of persuasion” 和 “principles and methods”。main purpose 題要抓整體研究方向，不要被例子拉走。

questions.answer: C — He worked with and learnt from a range of salespeople.
questions.answerKey: C — He worked with and learnt from a range of salespeople.
questions.translation: 哪一句正確描述 Cialdini 的研究方法？

blocks.text: “Which statement correctly describes Cialdini’s research methodology?”
這題問 methodology，即他怎樣做研究。不要回答他研究了什麼 principle，也不要回答 towel experiment 的結果。要找方法、做法、資料來源。

“He found that laboratory experiments on the psychology of persuasion were telling only part of the story, so he began to research influence in the real world, enrolling in sales-training programmes: ‘I learnt how to sell automobiles from a car lot, how to sell insurance from an office, how to sell encyclopaedias door to door.’”
他發現實驗室中關於說服心理的實驗只能說明部分情況，所以他開始在真實世界中研究影響力，參加銷售訓練課程。他說自己學習如何在車行賣車、如何在辦公室賣保險、如何挨家挨戶賣百科全書。

“In Cialdini’s book ‘Yes! 50 Secrets from the Science of Persuasion’, co-written with another social scientist and a business consultant, he explains that guests were responding to the persuasive force of ‘social proof’, the idea that our decisions are strongly influenced by what we believe other people like us are doing.”
在 Cialdini 與另一位社會科學家和一位商業顧問合著的《Yes! 50 Secrets from the Science of Persuasion》中，他解釋住客是在回應 social proof 的說服力量，也就是我們的決定會強烈受到「像我們的人正在做什麼」這種信念影響。
首尾句顯示 Paragraph C 先講研究方法，再講 towel experiment 的結果。Question 2 問methodology，所以應停在第一句及其引號內容。
原文沒有 methodology 這個字，但有：
這些都是方法詞。Cialdini 的做法是進入真實銷售場景，向不同銷售訓練學習。
“he began to research influence in the real world, enrolling in sales-training programmes”
他開始在真實世界中研究影響力，參加銷售訓練課程。
“I learnt how to sell automobiles from a car lot, how to sell insurance from an office, how to sell encyclopaedias door to door.”
我學習如何在車行賣汽車，如何在辦公室賣保險，如何挨家挨戶賣百科全書。
這裡有三種銷售場景：汽車、保險、百科全書。它們支援 C 的 “a range of salespeople”。雖然原文說的是 sales-training programmes，不一定逐字說 “worked with salespeople”，但參加這些訓練並學習不同銷售方式，意思上就是從不同銷售行業中學習 influence techniques。
A He reviewed data in a large number of recent books.原文有 writing bestsellers 和 latest book，但沒有說他的方法是 review data in books。
B He conducted all his experiments in a laboratory.原文方向相反。Cialdini 發現 laboratory experiments 只說明部分情況，所以轉向 real world。
C He worked with and learnt from a range of salespeople.正確。原文的 car lot、insurance office、door-to-door encyclopaedias 對應 a range of sales settings。
D He made many telephone calls to collect information.文章只說訪問中他 was on the phone from London，不是研究方法。
enrolling in sales-training programmes= worked with / learnt from sales contexts automobiles / insurance / encyclopaedias= a range of salespeople / sales settings
B 很容易吸引學生，因為段首有 laboratory experiments。不過原文說 laboratory experiments were telling only part of the story。這句的功能是解釋他為何轉向 real-world research。看到familiar word 不夠，還要看句子方向。

questions.answer: C — More guests complied with a message about other guests’ behaviour than with one
questions.answerKey: C — More guests complied with a message about other guests’ behaviour than with one
questions.translation: 關於毛巾實驗，哪一句正確？

blocks.text: “Which statement about the towel experiment is correct?”

目標段落：Paragraph C第一句已經說 Cialdini 從實驗室走向 real world research。段落中段詳細講 hotels leave a card asking guests to reuse towels。最後一句點出 guests were responding to social proof。由首尾句和中間主題詞 towel、hotel、guests 可知，Question 3 必定在 Paragraph C。
“changed the card’s message from an environmental one…”
“the majority of guests at the hotel had reused their towel…”

“To test this, the researchers changed the card’s message from an environmental one to the simple (and truthful) statement that the majority of guests at the hotel had reused their towel at least once.”
為了測試這一點，研究人員把卡片上的訊息由環保訊息改成一個簡單而真實的說法：酒店大部分住客至少曾重用毛巾一次。
“Guests given this message were 26 per cent more likely to reuse their towels than those given the old message.”
收到這種訊息的住客，比收到舊訊息的住客重用毛巾的可能性高 26%。
這兩句合起來非常清楚：新訊息是 other guests’ behaviour，即大部分住客都重用毛巾；舊訊息是environmental message，即保護環境。結果是新訊息更有效。
A Different hotel guests responded in entirely different ways.原文沒有說 entirely different ways。它比較的是兩種卡片訊息的效果，不是不同住客類型之間完全不同。
B Most guests responded only to the environmental message.方向錯。原文說 social proof message 令重用率更高。
C More guests complied with a message about other guests’ behaviour than with one about protecting the environment.正確。這正是 26 per cent more likely 的意思。
D More guests followed the hotel’s original message.原文說 old message 效果較低，新的 majority-guests message 效果較高。
majority of guests at the hotel had reused their towel= other guests’ behaviour 26 per cent more likely to reuse= more guests complied environmental one= message about protecting the environment
最重要的中伏位是 environmental message。IELTS 常用常識吸引學生：環保訊息看似應該有效，但原文實驗結果顯示 social proof 更有效。這題要跟數據走，不要跟日常直覺走。

questions.answer: A — The way chocolates were presented affected diners’ tips.
questions.answerKey: A — The way chocolates were presented affected diners’ tips.
questions.translation: 餐廳朱古力實驗顯示了什麼？

blocks.text: “What did the restaurant chocolate experiment show?”
“So much for towels. Cialdini has also learnt a lot from confectionery.”
毛巾就說到這裡。Cialdini 也從糖果／朱古力中學到很多。
“This is ‘reciprocity’ in action: we want to return favours done to us, often without bothering to calculate the relative value of what is being received and given.”
這就是 reciprocity 的運作：我們想回報別人給我們的好處，而且常常不會仔細計算自己收到和付出的價值是否相等。
首尾句顯示這段用 confectionery / chocolate experiment 解釋 reciprocity。Question 4 問實驗顯示什麼，所以要看中間不同派朱古力方法和 tips 數字。
“The secret, it seems, is in how you give the chocolate.”
看來，關鍵在於你怎樣給朱古力。
“When the chocolates arrived in a heap with the bill, tips went up a miserly 3 per cent compared to when no chocolate was given.”
當朱古力和帳單一起成堆送來時，小費只比沒有朱古力時增加了可憐的 3%。
“But when the chocolates were dropped individually in front of each diner, tips went up 14 per cent.”
但當朱古力逐一放到每位食客面前時，小費上升了 14%。

“The scientific breakthrough, though, came when the waitress gave each diner one chocolate, headed away from the table then doubled back to give them one more each as if such generosity had only just occurred to her. Tips went up 23 per cent.”
真正的科學突破出現在另一種做法：女侍應先給每人一粒朱古力，離開桌子後又折返回來，好像突然想到要更慷慨一點，再給每人多一粒。小費上升了 23%。
三種 presentation 帶來不同 tips：3%、14%、23%。這直接支援 A。
A The way chocolates were presented affected diners’ tips.正確。原文的 “how you give the chocolate” 是答案核心。
B Regular customers tipped more than occasional customers.原文沒有比較 regular 和 occasional customers。
C People tipped only when they were offered chocolate.原文沒有 only。它比較 no chocolate 和不同 giving methods；不能推出沒有朱古力就沒人給小費。
D Providing chocolates with the bill produced the largest increase in tips.錯。with the bill 只有 3%，最大 increase 是 doubled back 的 23%。
how you give the chocolate= the way chocolates were presented tips went up 3 / 14 / 23 per cent= affected diners’ tips
D 最有迷惑性，因為 “with the bill” 確實出現了。不過它只帶來最小升幅。數字題要看比較方向： largest increase 是 23%，不是 3%。

questions.prompt: “Robert Cialdini experienced the principles of influence first-hand in real-life sales settings.”
questions.translation: Robert Cialdini 在真實銷售環境中親身體驗了影響力原理。

blocks.text: “He found that laboratory experiments on the psychology of persuasion were telling only part of the story, so he began to research influence in the real world, enrolling in sales-training programmes…”
他發現實驗室中關於說服心理的實驗只能說明部分情況，所以他開始在真實世界中研究影響力，參加銷售訓練課程。
最後一句講 social proof，屬於實驗結果。Question 5 問 real-life sales settings，所以重點在首句。
“I learnt how to sell automobiles from a car lot, how to sell insurance from an office, how to sell encyclopaedias door to door.”
我學習如何在車行賣汽車，如何在辦公室賣保險，如何挨家挨戶賣百科全書。
這句很清楚顯示他不是只閱讀理論，也不是只在 laboratory 做實驗。他走進真實銷售環境，學習不同銷售方式。題目的 “first-hand” 對應他親自 enrolled in sales-training programmes 並 “learnt how to sell”。

題目命題：主體：Robert Cialdini動作：experienced principles first-hand場景：real-life sales settings原文命題：主體：Cialdini動作：researched influence in the real world; enrolled in sales-training programmes; learnt how to sell場景：car lot, office, door to door比較結果：方向一致，所以答案是 TRUE。
experienced first-hand= enrolled in programmes and learnt how to sell real-life sales settings= car lot / office / door to door
題目說 principles of influence，原文在這句未直接說 six principles，但整段前後都在講 influence和 persuasion。first-hand 的證據來自 “I learnt how to sell…” 這種親身學習方式，所以 TRUE 成立。

questions.prompt: “The principles of persuasion differ from country to country.”
questions.translation: 說服原理會因國家不同而不同。

blocks.text: “Geeling Ng, operations manager at Auckland’s Soul Bar, says she’s never heard of Kiwi waiting staff using such a cynical trick, not least because New Zealand tipping culture is so different from that of the US…”
Auckland’s Soul Bar 的營運經理 Geeling Ng 說，她從未聽過新西蘭侍應使用這種刻意的技巧，尤其因為新西蘭的小費文化和美國很不同。
而且毫無疑問，也會轉化成顧客再次光臨。
首尾句顯示這段比較 New Zealand 和 US 的 tipping culture，但同時仍在 reciprocity 框架內。題目問 principles 是否不同，所以要細讀 “general principle” 這個詞。
“New Zealand tipping culture is so different from that of the US”
“But she certainly understands the general principle of reciprocity.”
“But she certainly understands the general principle of reciprocity.”
但她當然明白 reciprocity 這個一般原理。

這句的功能很重要。前面說 New Zealand tipping culture 和 US 不同，後面卻說她理解 general principle of reciprocity。也就是說，不同地方的文化反應和外在結果可以不同：美國可能變成instant tip；新西蘭可能變成 huge smile、thanks、return visits。可是 reciprocity 作為 general principle 仍然成立。
“In America, it would translate into an instant tip. In New Zealand, it translates into a huge smile and thanks to you. And, no doubt, into return visits.”
在美國，它會轉化成立即的小費；在新西蘭，它會轉化成燦爛的笑容和感謝，而且大概也會轉化成再次光顧。
題目說 principles differ from country to country。原文支持的是 tipping behaviour differs /expression differs，但 general principle remains reciprocity。題目把 cultural outcome 說成principle itself，方向不準確。
判斷：原文有明確相反方向：principle 是 general principle；不同的是 tipping culture 和外在反應。因此答案是 FALSE。
New Zealand tipping culture is different from US= 文化和小費習慣不同general principle of reciprocity= 原理仍然是互惠題目把 result / cultural practice改成 principle itself所以錯。
最大中伏位是 “different from that of the US”。學生看到 different 和 country，就可能選 TRUE。
可是要問不同的是什麼。原文說不同的是 tipping culture，不是 persuasion principles。真正控制答案的是 “general principle of reciprocity”。

questions.prompt: “In New Zealand, people tend to tip waiting staff after being served chocolate.”
questions.translation: 在新西蘭，人們被送上朱古力後，通常會給侍應小費。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph E第一句已經指出，新西蘭侍應未必使用朱古力技巧，因為 New Zealand tipping culture 和 US 很不同。最後一句說額外服務在新西蘭可能轉化成 return visits。題目問 New Zealand、tip、chocolate，因此明顯定位到 Paragraph E。
“If you did that in New Zealand…”
“In America, it would translate into an instant tip. In New Zealand, it translates into a huge smile and thanks…”
“If you did that in New Zealand, as diners were leaving they’d say, ‘Can we have some more?’”
如果你在新西蘭這樣做，食客離開時會說：「可以再給我們一些嗎？」這句已經帶有幽默語氣，指出在新西蘭，送朱古力未必會直接引發小費。更清楚的是：
“In America, it would translate into an instant tip. In New Zealand, it translates into a huge smile and thanks to you.”
在美國，它會轉化成立即的小費；在新西蘭，它會轉化成燦爛的笑容和感謝。
題目說 New Zealand people tend to tip waiting staff after chocolate。原文說 instant tip 是America 的情況；New Zealand 的結果是 smile and thanks，並可能 return visits。這不是缺資料，而是明確分配了不同地區的反應。
判斷：題目把 America 的結果放到 New Zealand，與原文相反，所以答案是 FALSE。
tend to tip= translate into an instant tip New Zealand原文對應：huge smile and thanks / return visits
這題最容易因 Paragraph D 的 tips went up 23 per cent 被影響。Paragraph D 是美國式 tipping context 的實驗；Paragraph E 轉到 New Zealand，明確說 tipping culture different。遇到跨段題，必須看地點是否一致。

questions.prompt: “Older New Zealanders are particularly responsive to extra restaurant service because of reciprocity.”
questions.translation: 年紀較大的新西蘭人因為互惠原理，對額外餐廳服務特別有反應。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph E這段講 New Zealand restaurant context、extra service 和 reciprocity。題目有 New Zealanders、extra restaurant service、reciprocity，所以 Paragraph E 是合理目標段落。可是題目還加入
“Older”，這是年齡限制，需要特別查找。
“give them something they’re not expecting in the way of service”
但沒有找到 older、elderly、age group、older diners、younger diners 之類資料。
“The way to a diner’s heart is ‘to give them something they’re not expecting in the way of service’.”
打動食客的方法，是在服務上給他們一些意料之外的東西。
“It might be something as small as leaving a mint on their plate, or it might be remembering that last time they were in they wanted their water with no ice and no lemon.”
這可以是小如在碟上留一粒薄荷糖，也可以是記得他們上次來時想要不加冰、不加檸檬的水。
這些句子支援 extra service 會引發正面反應，但沒有把反應限制到 older New Zealanders，也沒有比較 older 和 younger diners。題目的 “particularly” 也需要比較：年長者是否比其他人更有反應？原文完全沒有這類年齡比較。
判斷：原文有 New Zealand、extra service、reciprocity，但缺少 Older 和 particularly responsive。沒有明確相反資料，所以不是 FALSE；核心年齡資料缺失，所以答案是 NOT GIVEN。
原文有： extra service= give them something they’re not expecting positive response= smile, thanks, return visits原文缺： older New Zealanders particularly responsive age comparison
題目把真實資料和不存在的年齡限制混在一起。學生看到 reciprocity 和 extra service 都在Paragraph E，容易選 TRUE。可是 IELTS T/F/NG 要逐個元素檢查。缺少 age group，就不能判TRUE。

questions.translation: 專家向客戶展示自己的資格。

blocks.text: “Authority: We trust people who know what they’re talking about.”
權威：我們信任那些知道自己在說什麼的人。

“In one study, therapists whose patients wouldn’t do their exercises were advised to display their qualification certificates prominently. They did and experienced an immediate leap in patient compliance.”
在一項研究中，那些病人不肯做練習的治療師被建議把資格證書放在顯眼位置。他們這樣做後，病人的配合度立刻大幅上升。
首尾句直接定義 Authority，再以 qualification certificates 作例子。Question 9 幾乎是原文改寫。
“So inform people honestly of your credentials before you set out to influence them.”
所以在你開始影響別人之前，要誠實地告知別人你的資歷。
題目的 experts 對應 therapists / people with expertise；qualifications 對應 credentials /qualification certificates；clients 對應 patients。這是 authority principle，因為人們信任有專業知識或資格的人。
experts= people who know what they’re talking about / therapists qualifications= credentials / qualification certificates clients= patients
這題不要選 A。雖然展示資格可能帶來對方配合，但它不是互惠，也不是稀缺。真正觸發影響力的是 professional authority。

questions.prompt: “Parents point out that other children behave in the desired way.”
questions.translation: 父母指出其他孩子正在以理想方式行事。

blocks.text: “Social proof: We decide what to do by looking around to see what others just like us are doing.”
社會認同：我們會四處觀察與自己相似的人在做什麼，然後決定自己該怎樣做。
“More perniciously, social proof is the force underpinning the competitive materialism of‘keeping up with the Joneses’.”
較負面地說，social proof 也是「跟鄰居攀比」這種競爭性物質主義背後的力量。
首尾句顯示此段核心是 people follow similar others。題目中的 other children 正好對應 children looking sideways at other children。
“Find groups of children who are behaving in a way that you would like your child to”
“Find groups of children who are behaving in a way that you would like your child to, because the child looks to the side, rather than at you.”
找一些行為方式正是你希望自己孩子學習的孩子群體，因為孩子會看旁邊的人，而不是看你。
這就是 social proof。孩子不是單純因父母命令而改變，而是受到同輩或相似群體影響。題目
“other children behave in the desired way” 對應 “groups of children who are behaving in a way that you would like your child to”。
other children= groups of children desired way= in a way that you would like your child to point out / use as example= find groups for child to observe
不要選 C commitment。這裡沒有先前承諾，也沒有要求孩子保持一致。影響力來自「其他相似的人正在這樣做」。

questions.translation: 廣告商無情地利用供應有限這一點。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph F Paragraph F 先講 Reciprocity，後講 Scarcity。題目中的 limited availability 是 scarcity 的直接定義。
“Scarcity: People want more of things that are less available.”
“Advertisers ruthlessly exploit scarcity (‘limit four per customer’, ‘sale must end soon’)…”
“Scarcity: People want more of things that are less available.”
稀缺：人們更想得到那些較難取得的東西。
“Advertisers ruthlessly exploit scarcity (‘limit four per customer’, ‘sale must end soon’)…”
廣告商無情地利用稀缺感，例如「每位顧客限購四件」、「優惠快將結束」。
題目直接改寫這句。limited availability 對應 scarcity / less available。由於選項 A 把 Reciprocity or scarcity 放在一起，所以答案是 A。
limited availability= scarcity / less available advertisers exploit= advertisers ruthlessly exploit scarcity
A 這個選項同時包含 Reciprocity 和 Scarcity。Question 11 的實際 principle 是 scarcity，但因選項 A 把兩者合併，所以仍選 A。不要因 reciprocity 也在 A 裡就排除它。

questions.prompt: “A survey uses a name similar to that of the respondent.”
questions.translation: 一份問卷使用一個與受訪者相似的名字。

blocks.text: “Liking: We say yes more often to people we like.”
喜歡：我們更常答應自己喜歡的人。
“We favour people who resemble us, even if the resemblance is as minor as the sound of their name.”
我們會偏向和自己相似的人，即使相似之處只是名字的聲音。
首尾句明確表示，本段講 liking，並把 name resemblance 作為例子。Question 12 直接定位到這段。
“fake name resembling that of the subject”
“When the researcher gave a fake name resembling that of the subject (e.g., Cynthia Johnson is sent a survey by ‘Cindy Johansen’), surveys were twice as likely to be completed.”
當研究員使用一個與受試者名字相似的假名時，例如 Cynthia Johnson 收到由 “Cindy Johansen” 發出的問卷，問卷被完成的可能性高出一倍。
這是 liking principle 的一個奇怪但有力的例子。人會因為名字相似而產生微弱的親近感，於是更願意回覆問卷。
survey uses a name= researcher gave a fake name similar to respondent= resembling that of the subject answer / respond more= surveys were twice as likely to be completed
名字相似不等於 authority，也不等於 social proof。這裡沒有專業資格，也沒有「其他人都這樣做」。核心是 resemblance creates liking。

questions.prompt: “Colleagues are asked in advance whether they will offer support.”
questions.translation: 同事先被問到是否會提供支持。

blocks.text: “Commitment/consistency: We want to act in a way that is consistent with the commitments we have already made.”
承諾／一致性：我們希望自己的行動與已作出的承諾一致。
“Later, return with the sponsorship form to those who said yes and remind them of their earlier commitment.”
之後，帶著贊助表格回到那些先前說 yes 的人面前，提醒他們早前作出的承諾。
首尾句顯示，本段完整說明先取得 commitment，之後利用 consistency 促成行動。Question 13的 in advance 是非常強的定位詞。
“First, ask workmates if they think they will sponsor you…”
“First, ask workmates if they think they will sponsor you on your egg-and-spoon marathon.”
首先，問同事是否認為他們會贊助你的持匙托蛋賽跑。
“Later, return with the sponsorship form to those who said yes and remind them of their earlier commitment.”
之後，帶著贊助表格回到那些說過 yes 的人面前，提醒他們早前作出的承諾。
這裡的 persuasion mechanism 很清楚：先讓對方作出初步答應，之後對方會想保持一致，所以更可能真正簽名或捐款。題目中的 “asked in advance whether they will offer support” 正是 “First, ask workmates…” 的改寫。
colleagues= workmates asked in advance= First, ask…offer support= sponsor you previous commitment= those who said yes / earlier commitment
不要選 reciprocity。這裡沒有先送禮物，也沒有要求對方回報。真正觸發行動的是「我之前已經說yes，所以現在最好保持一致」。

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：先用首尾句建立全文地圖
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 只看 Paragraph A 的開首，文章先用母親教人說 please 的例子，引出「說服別人」這個日常主題；最後一句則突然提到 Robert Cialdini 做毛巾實驗，並認為這能揭示社會如何運作。由首尾句可推測，這段主要是引言：先用輕鬆、熟悉的例子吸引讀者，再把焦點轉到一位研究 persuasion 的心理學家身上。這段未正式解釋實驗結果，主要功能是介紹人物、主題和文章語氣。

Paragraph B 第一指出 towel experiments 屬於 Cialdini 研究 how we persuade others to say yes的一部分；最後一句由 Cialdini 自述自己一直容易受 salespeople 和 fundraisers 說服，所以想知道原因。由首尾句可見，這段主要介紹 Cialdini 的研究目的：他想把 persuasion 的技巧系統化，理解為何某些人特別擅長令人答應。這段也提醒讀者，他研究的目標不只是銷售技巧，更是影響力背後的心理規律。

Paragraph C 開首說 Cialdini 發現實驗室研究只能說明部分情況，所以轉向 real world research，參加不同 sales-training programmes；最後一句總結 towel experiment 的意義：酒店住客受到social proof 影響，即我們會被「像我們的人正在做什麼」左右。由首尾句可推測，這段會先講研究方法，再用毛巾實驗展示其中一個 persuasion principle。這段對 Questions 2 和 3 特別重要，因為它同時包含 methodology 和 towel evidence。

Paragraph D 第一說 Cialdini 也從 confectionery，即糖果或朱古力，學到很多；最後一句明確點出reciprocity：人會想回報別人給自己的好處，甚至未必仔細計算雙方價值是否相等。只看首尾句已可估計，這段會用 restaurant chocolate experiment 說明互惠原理。中間數字如 3%、14%、23%很可能是細節證據。這段對 Question 4 很重要，因為題目問朱古力實驗顯示了什麼。

Paragraph E 開首引入 Auckland’s Soul Bar 的 operations manager Geeling Ng，指出新西蘭侍應未必會使用這種刻意的朱古力技巧，原因和 tipping culture 有關；最後一句說這些額外服務大概會帶來回頭客。首尾句顯示，這段主要把美國實驗放到 New Zealand culture 對照，說明同一個reciprocity principle 在不同文化中可能呈現不同結果。這段對 TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN 題很重要，特別是 New Zealand、tipping、extra service。

Paragraph F 是 “The Six Principles of Persuasion” 的開端，第一部分解釋 Reciprocity：人想回報曾經給予自己東西的人；後半轉到 Scarcity：人更想得到不容易取得的東西。從段落首尾可見，這段不是實驗敘述，而是原理列表。charities 放筆入信、超市免費試食、廣告說限購或限時，都是這兩個原理的應用例子。這段對 matching 題尤其重要，因為題目會把例子配回 principle。

Paragraph G 第一直接提出 Authority：我們信任那些看起來知道自己在說什麼的人；最後一句用therapists 展示 qualification certificates 後，病人 compliance 立刻上升作為證據。由首尾句可見，本段功能非常清晰：定義 authority principle，然後用專業資格展示如何增加信任和服從。這段對Question 9 幾乎是直接定位，因為題目中的 experts、qualifications、clients 全部對應這段的credentials、certificates 和 compliance。

Paragraph H 第一說 Commitment / consistency：人傾向按照自己已作出的承諾行事；最後一句給出 charity sponsorship 的例子，先問同事是否會支持，之後再帶表格回來提醒他們先前說過 yes。首尾句顯示，本段重點是「先取得口頭或初步承諾，再利用一致性讓對方跟進行動」。這段對Question 13 十分直接，因為題目說 colleagues are asked in advance whether they will offer support。

Paragraph I 第一提出 Liking：我們較常答應自己喜歡的人；最後一句進一步說，人甚至會偏向那些和自己相似的人，即使相似程度只是名字聲音接近。由首尾句可見，這段會先定義 liking principle，再用 survey fake-name study 展示相似性如何提升回覆率。這段對 Question 12 很重要，因為題目中的 similar name 和 respondent 正好對應研究中 researcher 的假名與受訪者名字相似。

Paragraph J 第一提出 Social proof：我們會觀察與自己相似的人在做什麼，再決定自己如何行動；最後一句補充較負面的例子，即 keeping up with the Joneses 背後的競爭性物質主義。由首尾句可見，這段主要解釋 peer behaviour 如何影響個人選擇。中間還有 parenting example：父母應找出行為良好的孩子群體，因為孩子會看旁邊的人。這段對 Question 10 很直接。
